items.title: [AINews] The No AI Slop Manifesto
items.author: swyx .ai
items.excerpt: Congrats to both llama.ccp and ggml for reaching 1.0 (declaring stability and removing 35 deprecated functions from llama.cpp’s public header) and with SGLang also announcing 1.0 at the recent SGLang Summit. However, today’s title story goes to the No AI Slop manifesto, which arose out of the conference discussions at AIE CODE and which Dex introduced in the closing keynote after cosignatures by many of the speakers at the conference. It seems Hacker News also liked it, voting it up to the front page today. We started this manifesto to offer a useful tool for discussion at work, and hope it gets used that way. items.title: datasette-cluster-map 0.19
items.excerpt: Release: datasette-cluster-map 0.19 One of the oldest Datasette plugins, and still one of my favorites. It now works with Datasette 1.0a42, and depends on the new datasette-leaflet to ensure OpenStreetMap tiles are requested with a referrer header. Here's a map of power plants owned by California's PG&E, also demonstrating Datasette's recently redesigned facets: Tags: datasette, geospatial, openstreetmap
items.why_it_matters: Minor Datasette plugin release for maps. Little bearing on our stack or client delivery.

items.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3
items.excerpt: Release: datasette-leaflet 0.3 OpenStreetMap have a very reasonable policy that hits to their hosted tile server should send a referrer header. Datasette table pages used the Referrer-Policy: no-referrer HTTP header, causing plugins that loaded tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate that policy. datasette-leaflet is the plugin that loads a bundled Leaflet so other Datasette plugins can depend on it. It now sets the referrer policy on the tile requests themselves to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, passing the host but not the full path to the page. Tags: leaflet, datasette, openstreetmap
items.why_it_matters: Small Datasette plugin fix for OpenStreetMap referrer policy. A mildly useful reminder about Referrer-Policy for map tiles, but niche.

items.title: ESLint Ends Paid Contributor Program as AI Upends Open Source Collaboration
items.author: Sarah Gooding
items.excerpt: From Rust to Godot and curl, open source projects are tightening contribution rules as AI-generated code strains maintainers and changes how developers collaborate.
items.why_it_matters: Major OSS projects like ESLint, Rust and curl are tightening contribution rules over AI-generated code. This affects how our agent-assisted engineers contribute upstream and maintain dependencies.
